chapter: Jam sessions, pay and the Vanguard (corrected typing)
title: The Village Vanguard: Lion of Trinidad and Pearl Bailey
summary: Hodes played the Vanguard with Max Kaminsky and Wild Bill Davison and heard the Lion of Trinidad. He recalls Pearl Bailey and Max Gordon, who later paid her $1500 for the same act.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: This is how impressed you get, when you make the New York scene. That's it. So these were the early struggles in New York, until you start getting a few other breaks. Village Vanguard was a break. You go in there with your own trio, and I went in there with Max Kaminsky and Freddy Moore and then I came back or either extended the engagement when Max had left with Wild Bill Davison and Freddy Moore, working off as the group -- the Lion of Trinidad, who was a calypso innovator, and writer. He wrote that tune, 'never marry a woman prettier than you if you want to be happy and have a good life, always pick an ugly woman for your wife.'

So he was there. Pearl Bailey -- I saw Pearl Bailey on that floor, she was making either $40 or $75 a week. And Max Gordon, the big impresario, standing in the back with me, saying, I don't know what's wrong with that gal, there's something I can quite figure out. You know what he figured out? He bought the Blue Angel on the East Side with a partner, and within a couple of years, he's paying Pearl Bailey $1500 a week, and she hasn't changed a bit of that act. That's what he figured out.
She came in doing the same act. He just didn't understand it. For $75 a week, he couldn't understand it.

For $1500, he thought -- this is what tickles me about people that know. Pearl was a natural, she knocked me out, getting out in the middle of the floor, doing, 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary.' And she had a way of -- like, her brother was a great dancer. Her hands would keep a beat, her little palm, she palmed the beat with her hands. And it was just a pleasure to play for her and watch her.
So those were the kind of people that were in the Vanguard.
